unsupported_consumers.archive/041: folder chip names use a BG tilemap parser, not the shared raster parser; F9 >= E5 terminates; VRAM glyph allocation/other callers remain open
unsupported_consumers.NAME: three single-byte glyph indexes from a 32-bit packed value; four-byte F9FC stream is not supported; save producer and menu name input remain to be extended
unsupported_consumers.all_other_short_scripts: requires explicit producer/decoder/buffer/font evidence before adoption

policy: fail before compiler or ROM output for unclassified selection; no silent partial name

consumer_notes.key-item-name: archive 62 is read at seven places: five call the tile renderer 0x08053A04 (IWRAM 0x0300677C, whose F9 slot the menu extension already routes to the Hangul handler), one is the item-name table at 0x0804FA68 used by the dialogue name insert (64-byte buffer), and 0x08032E10/0x08032E64 has no caller anywhere in the ROM (direct or pointer) and is treated as dead code. Cell budget is the source length.
consumer_notes.shared-tile-place: archive 13 is read only at 0x0802DDF0, five calls of the tile renderer 0x08053A04 whose F9 slot routes Hangul; names keep the underscore padding that right-aligns the 13-cell PLACE field
consumer_notes.shared-tile-network: NETWORK menu (PET つうしん) labels of archive 1; every listed script was observed going through the tile renderer 0x0300677C (caller 0x08053A1A, F9 slot routes Hangul) with the user save, runs analysis/runtime/user_save_network_02..04. 187 and 193 (not shown with that save) are excluded
consumer_notes.link-row-parser: archive 1 script 177 is read only at 0x0802F0E8 (call 0x0802F0E4 from 0x0803D074, link-cable screen); the chip folder extension moves that call (window 0x0802F0F4/0x0802F0BC) to a copy of its F9FC row renderer, and the same screen family gets the cache reset at its font upload. Not runtime-tested (needs a link partner)
consumer_notes.command-bearing-labels: archive/013/script/242 (BUG PIECE counter, printBuffer + コ) and archive/001/script/179 (match record, printBuffer between 戦 and 勝) list their literals; the builder swaps each literal in place and checks the bytes, because TextPet reads a script that opens with F1 back as mmbn4
consumer_notes.archive-005-all: archive 5 has three claims: 0x0802F4B0 (folder name by index r7) and 0x0803CE3E/0x0804C3A6 (script 10 fixed, link screens); all call the tile renderer 0x08053A04 with eight cells, whose F9 slot routes Hangul. Scripts 2..7 share the index path proven for 0/1; リュック follows the dialogue word 가방
consumer_notes.program-name: archive 11 (Navi Customizer program names) has ten claims: eight load it for the tile renderer 0x08053A04 directly or through 0x08034148 (both route F9 to the Hangul handler), two sit in the item-name table at 0x0804FA68 used by the dialogue name insert (64-byte buffer), the same path as archive 62. Cell budget is the source length
consumer_notes.shared-tile-status: ROCKMAN status screen (PET ロックマン) labels of archive 1, each observed through the tile renderer 0x0300677C with the user save (analysis/runtime/user_save_rockman_01); 73 is aliased by 72 and 140 by 134..139. Number columns keep the source cell positions. 141..149 (other charge kinds) were not shown with that save and stay source
consumer_notes.shared-tile-library: DATA LIBRARY tab headers of archive 1 (120..123, 125), each observed through the tile renderer 0x0300677C with the user save while switching tabs (analysis/runtime/user_save_library_01)
consumer_notes.mail-header-name: archive 6 (LZ77, decoded to the moved buffer 0x0202C800) FROM/TO names; read by the tile renderer 0x030067A0 (analysis/runtime/user_save_mail_read_01); names keep the underscore padding of their field
consumer_notes.mail-subject: archive 6 SUBJECT lines; read by the ROM proportional renderer loop 0x08053BBE, whose F9 slot is routed to the Hangul hook in tools/rom_renderer_hangul.py
consumer_notes.credits-rom-renderer: archive 792 (staff credits, raw) has one claim (0x081103E0) used at 0x08110270, the only call of the ROM proportional renderer style-1 entry 0x08053A28; its F9 slot routes to tools/rom_renderer_hangul.py. Names are transliterated (국립국어원 일본어 표기) and right-aligned by leading spaces like the source. Not runtime-tested (end of game)
consumer_notes.save-screen-count: archive 1 script 12 (枚 after the battle-chip count on the SAVE screen) was drawn through the tile renderer 0x0300677C in analysis/runtime/user_save_network_03 (scripts 6..14 on the save screen); user screenshot 2026-10-04 showed it untranslated
consumer_notes.battle-enemy-name: archive 49 (enemy names) is a private clone for the battle name list (0x080166D4/0x0801687C, tile renderer with native style 0x0868E224) and the dialogue name-insert table (0x0804FA84); the three BG-parser readers (0x0803BF4C, 0x0803F5D8, 0x08040228) keep the Japanese source. User screenshot 2026-10-04 showed the battle list untranslated. Not runtime-tested yet (needs a battle)
consumer_notes.pet-label-tile-or-message: archive 1 remaining labels: archive-1 claims go to the tile renderer 0x08053A04 or the message box 0x0804DFA0/0x0804E2A4 (Hangul); the BG parsers read only script 177 (moved to the Hangul row renderer) and 199 (left in Japanese)
consumer_notes.message-box-pet: archive 2 is read only through the message box 0x0804DFA0 (0x080347A6, 0x0803F854, 0x08040468) and 0x080347CC; texts mirror the archive-1 wording; the message box reads the archive in place, so there is no byte cap (only the source cell count)
consumer_notes.tile-and-message: archives 12 and 58: tile renderer 0x08053A04 and message box 0x0804E2A4, plus the dialogue item-name table
consumer_notes.dialogue-insert-word: archive 16 (64 bytes per word copied to 0x0200B4D0 at 0x0804FB96 for the dialogue insert) and archive 635 (dialogue item-name table 0x0804FA88); wording follows the story lines that quote these words; budget is the 64-byte buffer (16 syllables), not the source cell count
consumer_notes.shared-tile-training: Operation Battle (training) menu labels, archive red 4 / blue 3 (the two revisions swap 3 and 4), decoded to 0x02028000 by 0x080406C2; scripts 0..2 are drawn by 0x080411B4 -> tile renderer 0x08053A04 with native style 0x086C6E60, whose F9 slot routes Hangul. The Mr. Famous lines of the same archive are story records
consumer_notes.shared-tile-shop: shop stock counter (printBuffer + コ) of the nine shop archives 31..39 listed by the shop table 0x08049BA0 (16-byte rows: archive, script base); every tile-renderer call of the shop screen (0x0804A550..0x0804A7C6) passes native style 0x086C6E60, whose F9 slot routes Hangul. Archives 111 and 223 hold the same counter at script 34 but are area archives read through other tables, so they stay untranslated until their reader is observed. Added later: 111/223 script 34 (same counter in two area archives); their reader was not isolated, adopted on the same whole-ROM evidence as map-area-label (every tile-renderer call uses a Hangul-routed style)
consumer_notes.shared-tile-bbs-list: BBS post list rows (author 8 cells + title 13 cells in a 23-cell row) of the six list archives 19..29 (odd), decoded to 0x02026000; the board screen draws each row with the tile renderer 0x08053A04 at 0x08049666/0x08049980, 23 cells, native style 0x086C6E60 whose F9 slot routes Hangul. Placeholder rows (BBS0 .. XXXX) stay as they are
consumer_notes.shared-tile-pa-memo: library P.A memo (archive 15, decoded to 0x02028000 by 0x080374F6): 0x08109D88 draws script (P.A id - 0x140)*5 + n with the tile renderer 0x08053A04, 9 cells x 4 rows, native style 0x0868E224 whose F9 slot routes Hangul. Chip names follow the chip folder wording; codes are aligned one column after the longest name as in the source
consumer_notes.map-area-label: travel map area names, archive 61 scripts 22..31 (decoded to 0x02028000 by 0x0804332E). The drawing call was not isolated and the map screen was not reached with the available save; adopted because every text path in the ROM handles F9FC: all 86 direct calls of the tile renderer 0x08053A04 pass style 0x0868E224 or 0x086C6E60, the IWRAM copy 0x0300677C is reached only through that stub, and the message boxes and the ROM renderer table carry the Hangul handler. Labels keep the source cell count and its leading-space alignment; ANSA (no kana) stays
